summary: Ask whether a related row exists without multiplying results.
documentation: EXISTS yields 1 if its subquery produces at least one row and 0 otherwise. The selected values do not matter, including NULL. A correlated subquery can test each row of an outer query.
inputs: A subquery, optionally referring to an outer row.
caution: A join can duplicate outer records when several related rows match. EXISTS is appropriate when only presence matters.
scenarios: List customers with any unpaid invoice.
Find products that have at least one stock movement.
Select event registrants with an attendance record.
title: Find customers with unpaid invoices
problem: Tables customers(id INTEGER, name TEXT) and invoices(id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, paid INTEGER). Return customer id and name once per customer having at least one invoice with paid = 0. Ignore paid = 1 or NULL, unmatched invoices and customers without invoices. Order by customer id.
goal: Use EXISTS or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Correlate an EXISTS subquery on customer_id and require paid = 0.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT or WITH query using the provided tables.
SELECT 1;
